questions.prompt: What observation of Russell's (1927) motivates Russellian monism?

options.text: Physics describes only structure and relations, never the intrinsic nature of matter

options.why_wrong: Russellian monism does not rest on quantum measurement.

options.text: Matter is ultimately made of ideas
Consciousness emerges at a threshold of complexity
options.why_wrong: Russellian monism rejects emergence from the wholly non-experiential.

questions.explanation: Physics tells us what matter does, not what it is; the one place we know anything intrinsic about the physical is our own experience. So the intrinsic nature of matter might be experiential or proto-experiential.

sources.citation: Russell, B. (1927). The Analysis of Matter. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner.
Goff, P. (2017). Consciousness and Fundamental Reality. Oxford University Press.

questions.prompt: What is the combination problem for panpsychism?

options.text: How to measure experience in fundamental particles
options.why_wrong: The problem is conceptual, not one of measurement.

options.text: How micro-level experiences could combine into a single unified consciousness like ours
How non-physical minds could move physical bodies
options.why_wrong: That is the interaction problem for substance dualism.

options.text: How consciousness could emerge from non-experiential matter
options.why_wrong: Panpsychism is meant to avoid that problem.

questions.explanation: Even if electrons have tiny flecks of experience, it is unclear how many such subjects add up to one subject with one point of view. James raised a version in 1890; until it is answered, critics argue, panpsychism relocates the hard problem rather than solving it.

sources.citation: Chalmers, D. J. (2016). The combination problem for panpsychism. In G. Brüntrup and L. Jaskolla (eds.), Panpsychism: Contemporary Perspectives. Oxford University Press.
James, W. (1890). The Principles of Psychology, Vol. 1, Chapter 6. New York: Henry Holt.

questions.prompt: Why does Galen Strawson (2006) argue that 'realistic' physicalism entails panpsychism?

options.why_wrong: The argument does not rest on quantum physics.
Causal closure is the premise of the exclusion argument, not Strawson's.

options.text: Because experience cannot emerge from the wholly non-experiential
Because the PhilPapers survey favours it
options.why_wrong: The argument is a priori, not sociological.

questions.explanation: Strawson holds that genuine emergence of experience from wholly non-experiential stuff is unintelligible, so a physicalist who takes experience to be real must place experiential being at the fundamental level. Critics take this to be a reductio of the emergence premise.

sources.citation: Strawson, G. (2006). Realistic monism: why physicalism entails panpsychism. Journal of Consciousness Studies 13(10-11), 3-31.
